scope: Mevalonate kinase deficiency, from hyper-IgD syndrome to mevalonic aciduria.

keyRecommendations.text: HIDS and mevalonic aciduria are the two ends of one spectrum caused by mevalonate kinase deficiency.
In HIDS the picture is febrile attacks; a subgroup also has neurological abnormalities.
Raised IgD and, in most patients, IgA, plus increased urinary mevalonic acid, support the diagnosis, which is confirmed by low enzyme activity or a disease-causing mutation.

clinicalBottomLine: Hyper-IgD syndrome is the milder end of mevalonate kinase deficiency: periodic fever, usually high IgD and IgA, mevalonic acid in urine, and confirmation by enzyme assay or genotype.
notableCaveats: Anakinra is mentioned in the full text but dosing recommendations from later series are not used here.
